title: Priority scoring and escalation ladder for dedicated reservations and SLA negotiations
creator: Sana Patel
description: Create a defensible, auditable priority scoring rubric and escalation ladder for enterprise Dedicated reservations. This ticket covers: (1) a redesigned intake form focused on measurable signals (qps, p95, model family, KV-cache priming), (2) a numeric scoring matrix that maps customer signals to recommended GPU class, reserved throughput band, and suggested scaling policy, (3) a clear two-stage escalation ladder (operations -> capacity concierge -> solutions eng -> revenue ops) and SLA negotiation playbook, and (4) templated communications and decision records for auditability. Goal is to reduce cycle time for committed-reservation decisions from weeks to <72 hours for standard profiles while preserving safety for capacity planning.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form v2 deployed to customer-concierge with mandatory fields for workload fingerprint (token distribution, avg seq len, concurrency), acceptable SLO targets (p95 latency), and preferred model family
Scoring matrix implemented as a decision table in Confluence and validated against 30 historical intake records with >=85% match to expert recommendations
Escalation ladder documented with RACI, SLA for response times at each tier, and email/Slack templates for each outcome

Three GPU-class recommendations (light: A100-40/RTX, standard: A100-80/V100-equivalent, heavy: H100/4x) and three reserved throughput bands (burst, baseline, enterprise-committed) codified with cost delta estimates
A pilot run with two anchor customers completed and judged successful by Customer Success and Solutions Eng
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Agreed to favor signal-based scoring (qps, p95, model family) over subjective business justification to improve repeatability (recorded in meeting notes)
2026-03-02: Opted for three coarse GPU-class bins to keep operations simple; rejected per-model micro-binning due to operational overhead
2026-03-05: Decided that burst credits will be time-limited (30m windows) and require explicit billing opt-in; legal requested billing language (ticket LEG-44)
2026-03-10: Chose a two-tier escalation ladder (concierge -> solutions-eng) for typical cases and full revenue-ops loop for contract exceptions

risks: Overly conservative scoring could lead to unnecessary reserved spend for customers
Billing/legal language for burst credits may delay rollout
Edge workloads (real-time streaming with 1-token responses) might be misclassified by coarse bins
